ts13.title: TS 1.3 cheatsheet: subagent invocation and context
ts13.picture: The coordinator is a project manager who can only send emails to contractors. A contractor sees just the email, never the manager's inbox, and sends back only a final report. Leave the facts out of the email and the work is wrong.
ts13.flowAlt: Flow: a coordinator with the spawn tool in allowedTools sends all independent spawn calls in one response; each subagent knows only its own system prompt, the prompt string and its tools; only the final message returns; the coordinator checks for gaps and re-delegates.
ts13.toolsAlt: Worked example: tools = [Read, Grep] on the subagent and allowedTools = [Read, Write] on the query. Read runs at once, Grep runs after approval, Write cannot be called.
ts13.perspectiveAlt: One tool call seen from the coordinator and from the subagent: Gate 1 is whether the tool is in the subagent's tools, Gate 2 is whether it is pre-approved.

rows: Can it spawn?
The spawn tool must be in the coordinator's allowedTools (Task on the exam, Agent in current docs).
Subagents defined but the tool is not listed: nothing errors, the coordinator answers alone, unsourced.
What does the subagent know?
Only its own system prompt and the prompt string you write. No history, no shared memory.
"The coordinator already has the findings." The subagent does not.
How is it set up?
An AgentDefinition: description (when to use it), system prompt (its role), tool restrictions (tools).
Mixing up tools (what it can SEE) with allowedTools (what runs WITHOUT ASKING).
How do I pass context?
Complete findings in the prompt, in a structured format: claim, source URL, document, page.
A prose summary loses the sources.
How do I run several at once?
Emit all independent spawn calls in ONE response.
One spawn per turn: slower, same result.
How do I write the prompt?
Goals and quality criteria, not step-by-step procedures.
Rigid checklists break when the case differs.
How do I explore alternatives?
Fork the session from a shared analysis baseline.
Re-running the whole analysis for each option.

coordinator: **allowedTools = [Task, Read, Write]** is set on the query. It answers one question only: which tools run without asking.
**Task is in the list** so the coordinator can spawn subagents (the exam names this requirement).
**It adds and removes nothing.** Listing Write there does not give any subagent a Write tool.
**Permission rules are inherited** by the subagent it spawns, so the same pre-approvals apply inside it.
subagent: **tools = [Read, Grep]** is set on its AgentDefinition. It is the only list that decides what the subagent can see.
**Write is not in its session at all**, so a call to it cannot happen, whatever the coordinator pre-approved.
**Grep is visible but not pre-approved**, so a call goes through the normal approval path (permission mode or canUseTool).
**Leave tools out entirely** and the subagent inherits every tool available to subagents.
sides.habit: To limit what a subagent can do, change tools on its AgentDefinition. Editing allowedTools will not restrict it.

rows: Its own system prompt (AgentDefinition prompt) and the spawn tool's prompt string
The parent's conversation history or tool results
Project CLAUDE.md files (unless the definition sets omitClaudeMd)
Preloaded skill content, unless listed in skills
Its tool definitions (all available, or only those in tools)
The parent's system prompt
A
No spawn tool in allowedTools
Nothing callable; the coordinator answers alone, unsourced.
B
Assume subagents inherit context
It starts fresh: only the prompt reaches it.
C
Always run the full pipeline
One-fact questions pay for three subagents; broad ones never decompose.
D
Decompose too narrowly
Every subagent succeeds, yet the report covers a third of the topic.
E
One spawn call per turn
Independent work is serialised: more turns, more time.
F
Route results around the coordinator
The coordinator is blind to failures and cannot handle errors.
G
No gap review or re-delegation
A missing area is never noticed.
H
Return the whole subagent transcript
Context balloons, defeating isolation (docs only, not in the guide).

ts13.wrongNote: A to G are exam topics. H comes from the official docs only.
plan: **Read** the Subagents concept page: summary, mental model, the receives table (15 min).
**Run the lab** variants A, B, E and the correct one; watch each distractor fail (25 min).
**Play** the Isolated context, Spawn tool and Parallel spawning tabs; predict before you press Send (15 min).
**Practice** the 24 TS 1.3 questions, aim for 80% or better; log which of the seven questions each miss hit (30 min).
**Next day:** redo only your misses, then 5 questions from TS 1.2, which overlaps on isolated context.
